output.brief: Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump comes from the storage compaction tuning pushed on the evening of 2 Nov. Compaction threads went from 2 to 6, disks went to about 97% busy within 5 minutes in every cell, and node-side read time rose from 61 to 262 ms. Per cell, p99 rose minutes after that push, not when each cell's gateway upgrade arrived. For example, use-1 got 5.8 at 22:05 but only degraded at 23:40, right after the push. The cell that skipped the push (aps-3) got 5.8 and stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. Network and traffic growth don't explain the pattern. Rolling back would reopen the security hole and wouldn't fix latency. Next step: revert the compaction tuning in one cell, watch p99 and backlog, then extend it if it works. Backlog is about 4% and projected to stay under 15% until at least 13 Nov, so there is room to do this carefully. Do not pause compaction fleet-wide. Hold off on rate-limiting Orrin until the 10 Nov backlog attribution is in. Confidence is high on the cause and lower on what drove the backlog growth.
